experiment: unique-candidate matched visual N128 scaling stress test

candidate_pool.grid: grasp x offset by wrist yaw, shuffled independently by locked scene seed

causal_comparison: visual_world_model minus matched_no_vision; same checkpoint and candidate inputs, visual latent is the only ablation
verdict: The N64 visual advantage does not continue at N128. Both learned arms select one successful program in 20 pools overall and one in 10 intended-slice pools, while every pool contains a success. More candidates worsen both learned selectors and provide no visual advantage.
limitation: This is a geometric stress grid over grasp offset and yaw on the same 20 scenes, not additional independent scenes or a natural-program diversity benchmark.
